concepts.title: The Roman Empire: Extent, Administration and Army
concepts.definition: The Roman Empire of Augustus and his successors spanned Europe, North Africa and Western Asia around the Mediterranean called 'our sea', governed through provinces under senators and emperors with a professional army of legions guarding the frontiers.
concepts.key_idea: The empire rested on cities, taxation, law and the army, and bestowal of citizenship spread Roman identity from Italy to the provinces.

concepts.title: Society, Economy and Slavery in the Roman World
concepts.definition: Roman society was stratified into elites, middling groups and lower classes with slaves at the bottom, whose labour ran mines, estates and households, while the economy rested on agriculture, long distance trade in wine, olive oil and grain, and monetary exchange across the empire.
concepts.key_idea: Slavery was a fundamental institution of the Roman economy, and much of the labour force in agriculture and mines came from war captives and traders.

concepts.title: Late Roman Crisis, Christianity and the Third Century
concepts.definition: From the third century the empire faced invasions, civil wars, plague and monetary crisis, Constantine founded Constantinople as a second capital and recognised Christianity, and the empire split into eastern and western halves with the western empire falling in the fifth century.
concepts.key_idea: Christianity spread through the empire's cities and became a state religion, reshaping late Roman society while Germanic settlements carved the western provinces.
